subject: Post-call alignment: CustOps POC acceptance criteria, metrics, and access checklist
message_1_subject: Post-call alignment: CustOps POC acceptance criteria, metrics, and access checklist
message_1_body:
Hi Maya — thanks again for the productive call this morning. Recap below plus proposed next steps so we can start the POC on May 3 (target).

TL;DR
- Agreed pilot scope: evaluate Redwood inference for CustOps’ ticket summarization use case (batch and live chat).
- Success metrics: 1) 90% F1 on summary extractive labels on your 1k eval set; 2) 95th percentile latency <= 220ms for live chat at 4 RPS; 3) token cost < $0.0009/token on avg for bursty workload via batching & KV cache.

Key pain points you reiterated:
- Erratic latency during peak support hours (spikes to 800ms) impacting agent handoff.
- Cost unpredictability when scaling to multiple regions.
- Need to keep PII inside VPC and strict audit logs.

Proposed POC scope (31-day):
- Day 0–4: Access & infra setup (service account, S3 sample data ingest, IP allowlist).
- Day 5–14: Prompt set creation + 1k labeled eval run (we’ll provide template prompts; you’ll confirm labels).
- Day 15–24: Load tests (steady 4 RPS and burst to 12 RPS) + latency/cost profiling.
- Day 25–31: Acceptance evaluation and handoff recommendation.

Owners (initial):
- Redwood: Rishi (AC), Aditya (runtime/ops), Monica (customer success & evals).
- CustOps: Maya (POC owner), Anil Kumar (infra lead).

Immediate asks from CustOps to unblock setup:
1) Create a read-only S3 bucket with 3 sample conversation files and share ARN + role/creds.
2) Add rishi@redwoodinference.com and aditya_rao@redwoodinference.com to your allowlist (IP ranges will follow).
3) Fill the attached short security questionnaire if possible (network egress & retention column).

Attachments: CUSTOPS_POC_SCOPE_v0.3.pdf (draft scope), custops-network-egress-instructions.docx (egress + firewall requirements).

Next steps I propose:
- Maya confirms availability for May 3 kickoff and provides S3 ARN and Anil’s contact by EOD Wednesday (Apr 21).
- Redwood to share a lightweight runbook for prompt packaging and an eval template by Apr 22.

Thanks — I’ll wait for the S3 details and Anil’s info and will schedule a 30-min kickoff once we have them.

Best,
Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

message_2_subject: Re: Post-call alignment: CustOps POC acceptance criteria, metrics, and access checklist
message_2_body:
Thanks Rishi — this is great and aligns with what we discussed. Quick notes: 

- May 3 kickoff works for us (I’ll block the calendar).
- I’ve asked Anil to provision a read-only S3 and he’ll share the ARN + an IAM role by EOD Apr 21.
- Security questionnaire: we’ll start filling it but may take 24–48h for full answers; expect partial return tomorrow.
- On metrics: latency target looks reasonable but can we include a fallback SLA (model variant fallback) if latency spikes during burst tests? We need automatic graceful degradation.

Looping in Anil so he has visibility.

—Maya
Maya Singh
Head of Product, CustOps AI
maya@custops.ai
message_3_subject: Internal: CustOps POC — infra & fallback plan
message_3_body:
Internal checklist for kickoff once we receive S3 + Anil contact: 

1) Infra prep (Aditya):
   - Prepare a VPC connector template and list of Redwood IP ranges for allowlisting.
   - Ensure Dedicated fallback plan available: pre-warm a smaller model variant (quantized) to use as automatic fallback if latency > 350ms for >10s during burst tests.

2) Eval & prompts (Monica):
   - I’ll share the 1k-label template and scoring notebook by Apr 22. Need a mapping of your evaluation labels (you suggested summary/concise/actionable).
   - Include a small prompt set to test hallucination cases (10 edge cases).

3) Cost profile (Rishi):
   - We’ll run an initial token-cost projection using batching + KV cache assumptions and send a cost envelope. Target average token cost < $0.0009, we’ll iterate if not hit.

4) Security
   - Send custops-network-egress-instructions.docx to Anil; confirm retention window (you mentioned 30 days).

5) Scheduling
   - Hold May 3 10:00–10:30 PT provisional for kickoff; I’ll send calendar invite once S3 ARN arrives.

I’ll draft an internal runbook for the engineer who joins the call so we can expedite access in-call.

Monica
message_4_subject: Re: Post-call alignment: CustOps POC acceptance criteria, metrics, and access checklist — kickoff next steps
message_4_body:
Thanks Maya / Anil — appreciate the quick turnaround. A couple clarifications before kickoff: 

- Fallback behavior: we will configure automatic routing to a quantized variant (lower-cost, lower-latency) when observed 95th percentile latency exceeds 300ms for >15s. That fallback is reversible and logged in the Console; Monica will add the rollback policy to the runbook.
- Data handling: short-term retention = 30 days confirmed unless you ask for a shorter window; we’ll enable audit logs for all request-level metadata.
- Access: when Anil shares the S3 ARN, please also paste the IAM role ARN so we can validate permissions. If there are any VPN constraints, let us know and Aditya will coordinate.

Action items for tomorrow (Apr 21):
- Anil: S3 ARN + IAM role + partial security questionnaire.
- Monica: eval template and prompt set draft.
- Aditya: VPC connector template and IP ranges (draft).
- Rishi: calendar invite for May 3 tentative kickoff (I’ll set it pending S3).

We’ll be standing by to join the kickoff and can provide an engineer for live troubleshooting.

Best,
Rishi
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
